scope: Public terminal/abandon/next-run commands, isolated formal ability progression, starting relic selection. Normal Boss victory and earned paid-upgrade gate remains B006b2; full save/replay B007 and external-agent audit B008 are not complete.
implementation: RunSettlementFlowService with owned RunSettlementContext and explicit isolated wallet callbacks; no global UI settlement or player wallet substitution.
run_return from a true Boss victory or ordinary defeat exposes run_settle; actual UTC start/settlement time feeds the same formal score and short-run multiplier.

Formal map abandon has no points; battle abandon uses the formal non-clear settlement and syncs only resolved persistent party members, without claiming unconfirmed loot. Both battle UI overlays use the same extracted party synchronization.
run_next retains session revision/request cache and isolated profile; replaces the owned map with the real shared bootstrap and chosen seed, clearing per-run locations/events/rewards.
Ability unlock/toggle is available only after a finished run and uses AbilityProgressionService. Initial ability bonuses and bags use the same formal bootstrap, acquisition and refresh services.

Default profile is session-specific and discarded on close. Explicit sanitized profileId persists in project-local Library/AgentAdventure/Profiles. Windows device names and path syntax are rejected. Deleting Library removes test profiles.
Full adventure crash-safe save, replay and durable cross-process idempotency are not claimed in this batch.

execution.mode: EditMode CLI and real HTTP host, -batchmode -nographics, NullGfxDevice
execution.isolation: All 12 batch-owned source/test/meta files hash-match original and validation copy. No scene save/restart or player persistence mutation performed in original project. Clone-only startup helper calls real server and exits on a marker; no gameplay overrides.

related.selection: Same 116 named related cases selected from final full-suite XML; this is not a separate final targeted test job.

initialRelatedRun.cause: Directed test used the map serialized elite reward table, which was not a configured pool, so the formal bag builder returned no choices.
initialRelatedRun.repair: Use the configured default treasure relic pool in the directed test; retain production builder behavior. Final full suite includes this passing test.
